Surah al-Shura (The Consultation)

Revealed in Makkah; its verses number fifty-three.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿Ayn Sin Qaf﴾ are two names for the surah, and for this reason they are separated from each other and counted as two verses. It has also been said: they are one name, and the separation is to match the rest of the Ha-Mim surahs. It is read as "Ha Mim Sin Qaf." According to the first view, they are two predicates of an omitted subject. It has also been said: "Ha" is the subject and "Ayn Sin Qaf" is its predicate; and according to the second view, the whole is a single predicate.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ is a resumptive statement (*kalam mustaʾnaf*) that comes to confirm that the content of this surah agrees with what is contained in the other revealed books sent down to the earlier messengers, in calling to monotheism (*al-tawhid*) and guiding to the truth. Or [it confirms] that its revelation is like its revelation after mentioning its name and drawing attention to the greatness of its status. The *kaf* (in *kadhalika*, "thus") is in the position of the accusative (*nasb*) as an object (*maf'ul*) of *yuhi* ("reveals") according to the first view, and as a qualifier (*naʿt*) of an emphatic verbal noun (*maṣdar*) of it according to the second view. *Dhalika* ("that") refers, according to the first view, to what is in it, and according to the second view, to its revelation, and the sense of distance in it [i.e., the use of *dhalika* rather than *hadha*] is to indicate the elevated rank of what is referred to and the great distance of its station in excellence. That is: like the meanings in this surah, He revealed to you in the other surahs and to those before you of the messengers in their books. The point of similarity is what has been referred to: the call to monotheism, guidance to the truth, and what contains the welfare of the servants in this life and the next. Or [it means] like its revelation: it was revealed to you at the time of the revelation of the other surahs, and to the other messengers at the time of the revelation of their books to them, not a revelation different from it. This is as in His saying: ﴿Indeed We have revealed to you just as We revealed to Noah﴾ and the rest of the verse. The basis of the similarity is that it comes through the angel. The form of the present tense (*al-mudariʿ*) is for narrating a past situation, to indicate the continuity of revelation and that the revelation of its like is His custom. In making the content of the surah, or its revelation, the thing compared to it, there is an exaltation of it that is not hidden. Likewise in describing Him, exalted is He, with the two attributes of might and wisdom. The delay of the agent (*al-fa'il*) is for observing the verse-endings (*fawasil*), along with what it contains of arousing eagerness. It has been read as *yuha* ("is revealed") in the passive form, on the basis that *kadhalika* is the subject (*mubtada'*) and *yuha* is its predicate (*khabar*), which is attributed to its pronoun, or [*kadhalika* is] an infinitive (*maṣdar*) and *yuha* is attributed to *ilayka* ("to you"), and *Allah* is raised (in the nominative) by what *yuha* indicates, as if it were said: "Who reveals?" So it was said: "Allah." *Al-ʿAziz al-Hakim* ("the Mighty, the Wise") are two qualifiers of Him, or a subject as in the reading *nuhi* (with the first person), and *al-ʿAziz* and what follows it are two predicates of it, or *al-ʿAziz al-Hakim* are two qualifiers of it.

(p-22) And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ are two predicates of "Lahu" (His). According to the aforementioned possibilities, it is a resumptive (istinaf) clause confirming His might (izzah) and wisdom (hikmah).

﴿The heavens are about to be torn apart﴾. It is also recited with a *yāʾ* (يَكادُ).

﴿yatafaṭṭarna﴾ (يَتَفَطَّرْنَ): they split apart, cracking from the greatness of Allah, exalted is He. It was also said that it is from the children's supplication to Him, as in Surah Maryam. It is also recited as *yanfaṭirna* (يَنْفَطِرْنَ). The first is more eloquent, because it is the *muṭāwiʿ* (the intransitive form, showing the result of an action) of *faṭṭara* (فَطَّرَ), whereas the second is the *muṭāwiʿ* of *faṭara* (فَطَرَ). It is also recited as *tatafaṭṭarna* (تَتَفَطَّرْنَ) with a *tāʾ*, to emphasise the feminine gender, and this is rare.

﴿from above them﴾: that is, the splitting begins from their upper direction. Singling out this direction, according to the first view, is because the greatest signs, and those most indicative of majesty and grandeur, come from that direction. According to the second view, it indicates that splitting from below them is even more fitting, since that monstrous utterance, when it had an effect from above, which is the sky, then it is even more fitting that it would have an effect from below. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the earth, since it carries the meaning of "the earths."

﴿and the angels glorify the praise of their Lord﴾: they declare Him far exalted above what is not fitting for Him, while joined with His praise.

﴿and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾: by striving in what would bring about their forgiveness, such as intercession, inspiration, and arranging the causes that bring one closer to obedience, and seeking the postponement of punishment in hope of the unbeliever's faith and the sinner's repentance. This encompasses both believer and unbeliever. Indeed, if *istighfār* (اسْتِغْفار, seeking forgiveness) were interpreted as striving to remove an anticipated defect, it would include animals and even inanimate things. Since it is restricted to believers, as in His saying ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾, what is meant by it is intercession.

﴿Surely Allah, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾: for no creature lacks a great share of His mercy, exalted is He. The verse, according to the first view, is a further confirmation of His greatness, exalted is He. According to the second view, it explains the perfection of His holiness above what is attributed to Him, and that His withholding the hastening of punishment for them over that monstrous utterance is due to the angels' seeking forgiveness, and His exceeding forgiveness and mercy. Thus it contains an allusion that He, exalted is He, accepts their seeking forgiveness and grants them mercy beyond what they asked for in forgiveness.

Surah 42, verse 6 (Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud, Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim):

﴿And those who take protectors besides Him﴾ — partners and equals.

﴿Allah is Watchful over them﴾ — Vigilant over their states and their deeds, so He will recompense them for them.

﴿And you are not a guardian over them﴾ — not one entrusted with them, nor one to whom their affair has been committed; your only duty is warning.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 7:

﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an.﴾ "ذَلِكَ" (dhalika) is a demonstrative referring to the verbal noun (*masdar*) of "أوْحَيْنا" (awhayna, "We revealed"), and the "ك" (kaf) is in the accusative position as an adverbial of manner (*maṣdariyya*). "قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا" (Qur'anan 'Arabiyyan) is the direct object (*maf'ul*) of "أوْحَيْنا". The meaning is: and like that wondrous, clear revelation that conveys meaning, We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, in which there is no confusion for you or for your people. It was also said that the demonstrative refers to the meaning of the preceding verse, that He, exalted is He, is the Guardian over them and you are only a warner. In that case the "ك" is the direct object of "أوْحَيْنا", and "قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا" is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from the direct object, meaning: We revealed it to you, and it is a clear Arabic Qur'an.

﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities﴾: that is, its people, and it is Makkah.

﴿and those around it﴾: from among the Arabs.

﴿and warn of the Day of Assembly﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection, because creation is gathered on it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿the Day He gathers you for the Day of Assembly﴾. It was also said: souls and bodies are gathered on it. It was also said: deeds and their doers. The verb "الإنْذار" (al-indhar, "warning") takes two objects, and the second may sometimes be introduced by "بِ" (bi). Here the second object of the first and the first object of the second have been omitted, for the sake of inspiring awe and suggesting generality. It is read "لِيُنْذِرَ" (liyundhira, with "ya") in which case its subject is a pronoun referring to the Qur'an.

﴿There is no doubt in it﴾: a parenthetical (*i'tiraḍ*) statement confirming what precedes it.

﴿A party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze﴾: that is, after their gathering at the place of standing, for they are gathered there first and then separated after the reckoning. The implied sense is: from among them a party, and the pronoun refers to those gathered, since the word "الجمع" (al-jam') indicates them. It is also read with both nouns in the accusative as circumstantial clauses (*hal*) from "them", meaning: and warn of the day of their gathering while they are dispersed, that is, approaching dispersal, or dispersed in the two abodes of reward and punishment.

ﷻ "And had Allah willed, He would have made them" — that is, in this world.

﴿a single nation﴾ It is said: [a nation] either guided or astray. This is an elaboration of what Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) summarized in his saying "upon one religion." So the meaning of His Exalted saying, ﴿but He admits whomever He wills into His mercy﴾, is that He, Exalted is He, admits into His mercy whomever He wills to admit into it, and admits into His punishment whomever He wills to admit into it. There is no doubt that His Exalted will regarding each of the two admissions follows the deserving of each of the two groups to enter its place. And it is certain that the difference between mercy and punishment necessarily entails a difference in the state of those who enter each of them. Therefore He did not will to make all of them one nation; rather He made them two groups. As for His saying ﴿and the wrongdoers have neither a protector nor a helper﴾, it was stated to indicate that admission into punishment comes from the side of those who enter it, by the requirement of their bad choice, and not from His side, Exalted is He, as is the case with admission into mercy. It is not for what has been said about exaggeration in the threat.

It is also said: [they are] all believers, and this is what Muqatil said: upon the religion of Islam, as in His Exalted saying: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾, and His Exalted saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾. The meaning is: had Allah willed a will of power, He would have compelled them to faith, but He willed a will of wisdom, and imposed obligations upon them and based their affair on what they choose, so that He would admit the believers into His mercy — and they are the ones intended by His saying ﴿He admits whomever He wills﴾ — and He left the wrongdoers without a protector or a helper.

And you know well that the supposition of making all of them believers is refuted by the opening of the exceptive transition with the admission of some of them into His mercy, since all of them would then be entering it; so the fitting thing then would be to open with the removal of some of them from among them and their admission into His punishment. What the context and the flow of the noble composition require is that the intended meaning be unity in disbelief, as in His Exalted saying: ﴿Mankind was one nation, then Allah sent the prophets﴾, the verse, according to one of the two interpretations, that they are those who were in the interval of Idris or in the interval of Nuh, peace be upon them both. So the meaning: had Allah willed, He would have made them one nation united upon disbelief, by not sending to them a messenger to warn them of what has been mentioned of the Day of Gathering and the various kinds of terrors in it, so that they would remain upon the disbelief they were in. But He admits whomever He wills into His mercy, i.e., it is His way that He sends to all someone who warns them of what has been mentioned, so some of them are affected by the warning and turn their choice toward the truth, and Allah grants them success in faith and obedience and admits them into His mercy; while others are not affected by it and persist in their error, and they are the wrongdoers, so they remain in this world (p-24) upon the disbelief they were in and in the Hereafter they come to the blaze, without a protector to manage their affair or a helper to rescue them from punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 9:

﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ This is a resumptive sentence (jumla mustan'afa), confirming what precedes it regarding the negation that the wrongdoers should have any protector (waliyy) or helper (nasir). "Am" (or) here is disjunctive (munqati'a), and what it contains of "bal" (rather) indicates a transition from explaining what came before to explaining what follows. The interrogative hamza is for denying the occurrence and negating it in the most emphatic and intensive manner, not for denying the actual event and condemning it, as has been said; for the intended meaning is to show that what they did is not at all a matter of taking protectors, because that is a branch of the idea that the idols are protectors, and this is among the most evident impossibilities. That is: rather, they have taken, beyond God, protectors from among the idols and others. Heaven forbid (hayhat).

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿So God, He is the Protector﴾ is the answer to an omitted conditional clause, as if it were said: after the invalidation of the protection of what they took as protectors, if they mean a protector in reality, then God, He is the Protector, and no protector other than Him.

﴿And He gives life to the dead﴾, that is: and it is among His attributes.

﴿And He is Powerful over everything﴾. Therefore He is the one worthy of being taken as protector; so let them single Him out for taking, rather than that which has no power over anything.

And whatever you differ about (﴿وَما اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾) is a quotation of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the believers: that is, whatever the disbelievers opposed you in concerning matters of religion, so that you and they differ.

﴿مُحْكَمَةٌ﴾ refers back to ﴿إلى اللَّهِ﴾ ("to Allah"), which means the rewarding of the righteous and the punishment of the wrongdoers.

﴿ذَلِكُمُ﴾ (That is) the Judge, the One of great standing.

﴿اللَّهُ رَبِّي﴾ (Allah is my Lord), my Master, ﴿عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ (upon Him I have relied) in the principal matters of my affairs, exclusively and not upon any other.

﴿وَإلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ﴾ (and to Him I turn back) I return, in every difficult matter that arises for me, to none other than Him. Since reliance (tawakkul) is a single, continuous matter, while turning back (inabah) is multiple and renewed according to the renewal of its occasions, the past tense form was chosen for the first and the present tense form for the second. It has also been said: "And whatever you differed about and disputed concerning any of the disputes, then refer it to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and do not prefer the judgment of anyone else over his judgment." It has also been said: "And whatever you differed about regarding the interpretation of a verse and it became unclear to you, then return in its clarification to the clear (muhkam) part of the Book of Allah and the apparent (zahir) part of the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." It has also been said: "And whatever disagreement arose among you concerning knowledge that does not relate to your obligations and for which you have no way to know, then say: Allah knows best, as with the knowledge of the Spirit (ruh)." There is no room to take this as referring to ijtihad (independent legal reasoning), since it is not permissible in the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 11:

﴿Fāṭir (Originator) of the heavens and the earth﴾ is either another predicate of "Dhalikum" (that is), or a predicate of an omitted subject, or a subject whose predicate is ﴿He has made for you﴾. It is also read in the genitive (Fāṭiri), in which case it is either a substitute (badal) for the pronoun, or an epithet (ṣifah) of the proper name ﴿Allah﴾ in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to Allah﴾, and what lies between them is a parenthetical insertion (i'tirāḍ) between the epithet and the thing described.

﴿From yourselves﴾ means from your own kind (jins).

﴿Mates (azwājan)﴾ means wives (nisā'an). The placing of the prepositional phrase before the direct object has had its purpose (sirr) explained more than once already.

﴿And of the cattle﴾ means: and He made for the cattle, from their own kind, ﴿mates (azwājan)﴾; or: He created for you from the cattle kinds (aṣnāfan), or males and females (dhukūran wa-inathan).

﴿He multiplies you (yadhra'ukum)﴾ means He increases you in number, from dhar' (scattering), which is dispersal; and in its meaning are dhar'u and dharr.

﴿Therein (fīhi)﴾ means: in that which has been mentioned of the arrangement (tadbīr), for the making of humans and cattle into mates results in breeding between them, like a source (manba') of dispersal and multiplication.

﴿There is nothing like unto Him (laysa kamithlihi shay'un)﴾ means: there is no one like Him in any of the matters, among which is this wondrous arrangement. What is meant by "His like" is His essence (dhāt), as in their saying, "One like you does not do such-and-such," intending to emphasize its negation from him, for when it is negated from one who is comparable to him, its negation from him is all the more fitting. Then this manner of speech was employed regarding one who has no like. It is also said: "His like" means His attribute (ṣifah), i.e., there is no attribute like His attribute.

﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing (al-samī' al-baṣīr)﴾: the one who is intensive in knowledge of everything that hears and sees.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 12:

﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is: their treasuries. ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills, and restricts it.﴾ He expands and constricts according to what His will requires, a will founded upon far-reaching wisdoms.

﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of all things.﴾ He is thorough in encompassing them, so He does everything in the manner in which it ought to be done. The sentence serves as a justification for what precedes it and as a preparation for what follows it, from His words, exalted is He:

﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾ It is a notification that what He prescribed for them proceeds from perfect knowledge and wisdom. Likewise, the attribution of this to those mentioned, upon them be prayers and peace, is an alert that it is an ancient religion on which all the messengers agreed, and the address is to his community, upon him be prayers and peace. That is: He prescribed for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and those after him from the possessors of sacred laws (ashab al-shara'i') and the Ulu al-'Azm (those of firm resolve) among the well-known prophets, upon them be prayers and peace, and commanded them to it with an emphatic command. The specification of them by mention is due to the elevation of their status, which was stated, and to win over the hearts of the disbelievers toward it, since all agree on the prophethood of some of them, while the Jews are alone in regard to Moses, peace be upon him, and the Christians are alone in regard to Jesus, peace be upon him. Otherwise, there is no prophet except that he is commanded with what He commanded him, and that is a reference to monotheism (tawhid) and the religion of Islam, and to what does not vary with the variation of nations and the change of ages among the fundamentals of the laws and rulings, as the mention of "enjoining" (tawsiya) indicates, for it expresses the emphasis of the command and the care for the matter commanded. As for the meaning of His revelation to him, upon him be prayers and peace, it is either what is mentioned at the beginning of the noble surah and in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus We have revealed﴾ and so on, or what encompasses those and others of what occurred in various other places, among which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith﴾ and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I am only a human like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is one God﴾ and other than that. The expression of that, when attributing it to him, upon him be prayers and peace, by "that which" (alladhi) is for increasing the magnification of his status from that aspect. The preference for "revealed" over what precedes and follows it, namely "enjoined," is to observe what occurred in the mentioned verses and because revelation contains an explicit statement of his messengerhood, upon him be prayers and peace, which suppresses the denial of the disbelievers. The shift to the plural of majesty (nun al-'azama) is to show the perfect care for his revelation, and this is the secret of placing it before what follows it, despite its precedence in time. The placing of the enjoining of Noah, peace be upon him, first is for hastening to explain that what is prescribed for them is an ancient religion. The turning of the address to him, upon him be prayers and peace, by way of talwin (shifting of address) is for honor and to alert that He, exalted is He, prescribed it for them through his tongue, upon him be prayers and peace.

﴿That you should establish the religion﴾ That is: the religion of Islam, which is the oneness of God, exalted is He, obedience to Him, belief in His books, His messengers, the Day of Recompense, and all that by which a man is a believer. The meaning of "establishing it" is correcting its pillars and preserving it from deviation, or persevering in it and striving for it. The position of "that you should establish" is either accusative, as a substitute (badal) for the object of "prescribed" and what is conjoined to it; or nominative, as an answer to a question arising from the vagueness of what was prescribed, as if it were said: "And what is that?" So it is said: "It is establishing the religion." It was also said that it is a substitute for the pronoun in "by it," but this is not so, because it, along with its leading to the removal of it from the scope of revelation to the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, necessitates that the address in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not be divided therein﴾ is to the mentioned prophets, peace be upon them, and directing the prohibition to their communities is an evident contrivance, together with the fact that the more apparent view is that it is directed to his community, upon him be prayers and peace, and that they are the ones who are divided, as you will be informed. That is: do not be divided in the religion, which is an expression of what was mentioned of the fundamentals, not the differing branches (furu') which vary according to the variation of nations with the variation of ages, as His saying, exalted is He, expresses: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is grievous to the polytheists﴾, which begins the explanation of the states of some of those to whom what was prescribed of the upright religion was prescribed; that is: it was great and burdensome upon them.

﴿What you call them to﴾ of monotheism and the abandonment of idol worship. They deemed it improbable, when they said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God chooses whom He wills to Himself﴾ is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) coming to establish the truth, and it contains an indication that among them are those who answer the call. That is: God draws to what you call them to whomever He wills to draw to Himself, and he is one who directs his choice to what he is called to, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, that is: whoever turns toward Him, since He supports him with success and subtle kindnesses.

The commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 14:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they did not become divided﴾ begins an explanation of the states of the People of the Book, following the general allusion to the states of the polytheists. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: They are the Jews and the Christians, because of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those who were given the Book did not become divided except after the clear proof had come to them﴾ (98:4). That is: they did not become divided over the religion to which they were called, and they did not believe as some of them believed.

﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ of its truth, through what they witnessed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Qur'an is among the proofs of its truth as they found it in their own Book; or [it refers to] knowledge of his (ﷺ) mission. This is an exceptive construction lacking its complement (istithna' mufarragh, an exception whose excluded item is not stated) from the most general of states or the most general of times. That is: they did not become divided in any state or at any time, except in the state of the coming of knowledge, or except at the time of the coming of knowledge.

﴿out of rebellion among themselves﴾ and zeal, and seeking leadership, not because they had some doubt [that justified it].

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, which is the promise to delay punishment,

﴿until a specified term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection,

﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾, meaning the judgment would have been carried out between them by their annihilation, since their crimes necessarily call for that without doubt. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed those who were made to inherit the Book after them﴾ ... etc., explains how the polytheists disbelieved in the Qur'an, following the explanation of how the People of the Book disbelieved. It is also read as "wa-rithu" and "wa-wurrithu," meaning: indeed the polytheists who were made to inherit the Qur'an after the Book was given to the People of the Book.

﴿are in disquieting doubt about it﴾ concerning the Qur'an,

﴿troubling﴾, causing unease or suspicion. For this reason they do not believe in it, not merely out of rebellion and obstinacy after they knew of its truth, as is the case with the People of the Two Books. This is [the explanation].

As for what has been said, that the pronoun in "they did not become divided" refers to the nations of the prophets, peace be upon them, and that what is meant is: each nation divided after its prophet, while knowing that division is misguidance and corruption and a matter threatened upon by the tongues of the prophets, peace be upon them, then this is refuted by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, until a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them﴾. Likewise, what has been said, that people were one community of believers after Allah, the Exalted, destroyed the people of the earth by the Flood, and when the fathers died the sons differed among themselves, and that this was when Allah, the Exalted, sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, and knowledge came to them, and they differed only out of rebellion among themselves. For the famous nations mentioned were struck by the punishment of annihilation without respite or reprieve. Moreover, the course of this noble composition is to explain the states of this Community. The prophets, peace be upon them, who were mentioned were mentioned only to establish that what was legislated for them is an ancient religion upon which those eminent figures, peace be upon them, all agreed, in order to emphasize the obligation of establishing it and to strengthen the restraint against division and disagreement concerning it. Therefore, addressing the explanation of their nations' division from it would perhaps give the impression of undermining that aim.

﴿Therefore﴾, that is, because of what has been mentioned of division and disquieting doubt, or because He has prescribed for them the upright, ancient, and true religion, worthy of being the object of eager competition by those who compete for it.

﴿So call﴾, that is, call all people to establishing that religion and acting in accordance with it. Their division, their being in disquieting doubt, and the prescribing of that religion for them through the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) are each a cause for calling to it and commanding it. The thing referred to is not the mentioned charge, the command to establish it, and the prohibition of division, so that the notion of mere repetition might be imagined. It has been said: the thing referred to is the prescribed religion itself, and the lam (la) here means "to," as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾ (99:5), meaning: so, to that religion, call.

﴿And be upright﴾ in it and in calling to it.

﴿as you have been commanded﴾ and as it has been revealed to you.

﴿And do not follow their desires﴾, the false ones.

﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Book God has sent down"﴾, any Book whatsoever among the revealed Books, unlike those who believed in some of them and disbelieved in others. In this there is an affirmation of the truth, a demonstration of the agreement of the Books in their fundamentals, a winning over of the hearts of the People of the Two Books (Ahl al-Kitab), and an indirect rebuke of them. The manner of believing in them has already been explained at the end of Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿And I have been commanded to be just among you﴾ in conveying the laws and rulings and in judging disputes when there is litigation and contention. It has been said: its meaning is: "There is no equivocation between me and you, I do not command you to what I do not do, I do not oppose you in what I forbid you, and I do not distinguish between your elders and your youngsters." The lam (la) is either in its literal sense, with the object of the command omitted, meaning: "I have been commanded with that in order to be just," or it is extra, meaning: "I have been commanded that I be just," with the ba' (bi) omitted.

﴿God is our Lord and your Lord﴾, that is, the Creator of us all and the Administrator of our affairs.

﴿For us are our deeds﴾, whose recompense does not pass us by, whether as reward or as punishment.

﴿And for you are your deeds﴾, whose effects do not pass beyond you, so that we benefit from your good deeds and are harmed by your evil deeds.

﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾, no disputation and no contention, because the truth has become manifest, no need for argument remains, and no place for opposition remains except obstinacy.

﴿God will gather us together﴾ on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And to Him is the final return﴾, whereupon our state and your state will become manifest there. This, as you see, is a restraining in the positions of answering, not an abandonment in the places of warfare, so that one would resort to abrogation (naskh) by the verse of fighting.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 16:**

﴿And those who dispute concerning God﴾, that is: concerning His religion.

﴿after it has been responded to﴾, after people have responded to it and entered into it. The expression of this as "responded to" is in view of their being called to it; or [it means] after God has responded to His Messenger ﷺ and supported him with His help; or after the People of the Book have responded to him, by acknowledging his prophethood (ﷺ) and seeking victory through him before his mission, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because the Jews and the Christians used to say to the believers: "Our Book is before your Book, our prophet is before your prophet, and we are better than you and more worthy of the truth."

﴿their argument is baseless (dahidah) in the sight of their Lord﴾, slippery, vanishing, false. Rather, they have no argument at all; and their falsehoods were only called an "argument" in accommodation to them, in accordance with their false claim.

﴿and upon them is wrath﴾, great, because of their obstinate rejection of the truth after its manifestation.

﴿and for them is a severe punishment﴾, whose extent cannot be measured.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 17:

﴿Allah is the One who sent down the Book﴾ i.e., the genus of the Book (jins al-kitab).

﴿with truth﴾ accompanied by it in its rulings and its reports, or with what it is fitting to send down of beliefs and rulings.

﴿and the Balance﴾ and the Sharia by which rights are weighed and people are made equal, or the very justice, by sending down the command to it, or the instrument of weighing (alat al-wazn).

﴿And what will make you know?﴾ i.e., what thing makes you aware?

﴿That the Hour﴾ which the Book speaking with truth informs of its coming.

﴿may be near﴾ i.e., a thing that is near, or its coming is near. It has been said: "near" is in the sense of "possessing nearness," or "the Hour" is in the sense of the Resurrection (al-ba'th). The meaning is: it is upon the wing of arrival, so follow the Book, act by it, and persevere in justice before the Day comes upon you suddenly, the Day on which deeds will be weighed and their recompense paid in full.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 18:

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ with the hastening of denial and mockery. They used to say: "When is it? Would that it would come, so that the truth may become manifest to us: is it that on which we are, or that on which Muhammad and his companions are?"

﴿But those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾ fearful of it, together with taking care of it, due to their expectation of reward.

﴿And they know that it is the truth﴾ i.e., that which is certainly going to occur.

﴿Verily, those who dispute concerning the Hour﴾ argue about it. It is from al-mirya (doubt, dispute), or from "maraytu al-naqah" when you rub its udder vigorously for milking, because each of the two disputants extracts what is in the other's possession by means of speech that carries intensity.

﴿are indeed in far-off error﴾ far from the truth. For resurrection is the most similar of the unseen matters to the perceptible ones, so whoever is not guided to accepting it is further and further away from being guided to what lies beyond it.

Allah is Subtle (Latif) with His servants: that is, He is Kind, exceedingly kind to them, bestowing upon them, through countless forms of His subtle kindnesses, what the hands of thoughts and conjectures can scarcely reach.

﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾: that He provides for him in whatever manner He wills, so He singles out each of His servants with a kind of kindness according to what His will requires, a will founded upon profound wisdoms.

﴿And He is the Strong﴾: the one whose power is overwhelming, who prevails over everything.

﴿the Mighty﴾: the Invincible, who cannot be overcome.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 20:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾ The ḥarth (tilth) is, originally, casting seed into the earth, and it is applied to the crop that results from it. It is used for the fruits and results of deeds by way of metaphor (isti'ara), based on likening them to the produce that comes from seeds, which implies a comparison of deeds. That is: whoever desires by his deeds the reward of the Hereafter.

﴿We will increase him in his tilth﴾ We will multiply his reward, from one to ten, up to seven hundred and more.

﴿And whoever desires﴾ by his deeds.

﴿the tilth of this world﴾ That is its goods and its pleasures.

﴿We will give him of it﴾ That is, some of it, according to what We have apportioned for him, not what he wishes and seeks.

﴿And he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ Since his aspiration is confined to this world. Its detailed explanation has already passed in surah al-Isra'.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 21:

﴿Or do they have partners﴾ That is: rather, do they have partners among the devils? The hamza here is for affirmation and rebuke.

﴿who have prescribed for them﴾ through enticement.

﴿of the religion that which Allah has not permitted﴾ such as polytheism, denying the resurrection, and working for the sake of this world. It is also said: their partners are their idols, and they are attributed to them because it was they who made them partners with Allah the Exalted, and the prescribing is ascribed to the idols because they were the cause of their misguidance and their being led astray, as in the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, they have led many astray﴾. Or the partners are the images of the one who established misguidance for them.

﴿And if not for the decisive word﴾ That is: the prior decree to delay the recompense, or the promise that the decision will take place on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿it would have been decided between them﴾ That is: between the disbelievers and the believers, or between the polytheists and their partners.

﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment﴾ It is also read with a fatha, coordinated with "the decisive word," meaning: and if not for the decisive word and the decree of the punishment of the wrongdoers in the Hereafter, it would have been decided between them in this world, for the painful punishment is dominant in the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 22:

﴿You will see the wrongdoers﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. The address is to everyone who is fit to receive it, with the aim of showing that the evil state of these people is not restricted to the sight of one particular beholder over another.

﴿Fearful﴾ (mushfiqin), i.e., afraid.

﴿Of what they earned﴾ (mimma kasabu), namely of the evil deeds.

﴿While it will surely befall them﴾ (wa huwa waqi'un bihim), i.e., its consequence (wabaluhu) will inevitably overtake them, whether they feared it or did not fear it. Or the clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in "mushfiqin", or it is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiradh).

﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds (p-30)﴾ ﴿in the gardens of the Gardens﴾ will be settled in the most pleasant and delightful of their precincts.

﴿For them is whatever they wish in the presence of their Lord﴾, i.e., whatever kinds of delights they desire will be theirs with their Lord. "In the presence of their Lord" (ʿinda rabbihim) is an adverbial complement (zarf) of the stabilized predicate (al-istiqrar al-'amil) in "for them" (lahum). It has also been said that it is an adverbial complement of "they wish" (yashaʾun).

﴿That﴾ (dhalika) is a demonstrative referring to what has been mentioned of the state of the believers, and the sense of distance contained in it serves to indicate the great elevation of the rank of what is pointed to.

﴿That is the great bounty﴾ (huwa al-fadl al-kabir), which its measure cannot be estimated and its utmost limit cannot be reached.

ذَلِكَ (That) is the great bounty, it is "that which Allah gives good news of to His servants" — meaning He gives them good news of it; the preposition was omitted and then the returning pronoun to the relative (al-ʿāʾid), as in His saying, ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ — or that bestowal of good news which Allah gives to His servants.

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ It is also read as "yubshiru" from abshara.

﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it.﴾ It is related that the polytheists gathered at one of their assemblies, and some of them said to others: "Do you think Muhammad asks a reward for what he undertakes?" Then this was revealed. That is: I do not ask of you, for what I am upon of conveying and giving good news, anything.

﴿Any reward﴾ — benefit.

﴿Except the affection among kinsfolk.﴾ That is: except that you show affection to me because of my kinship, or that you show affection to the people of my kinship. It has also been said: the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and the meaning is: I do not ask you for any reward at all, but I ask you for affection, and "among kinsfolk" (fī al-qurbā) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from it, that is: except affection that is established among kinsfolk and firmly rooted in its people, or in the right of kinship. And "al-qurbā" is a verbal noun like "al-zulfā," meaning kinship. It is related that when this was revealed, it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are your kinsfolk whose affection has become obligatory upon us?" He said: "ʿAlī, Fāṭima, and their two sons." And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Paradise is forbidden to whoever wrongs the People of my House and harms me regarding my ʿitra (family), and whoever does a favour to anyone of the descendants of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and does not repay it, I will repay him for it tomorrow when he meets me on the Day of Resurrection." It has also been said: al-qurbā means seeking nearness (al-taqarrub) to Allah, that is: except that you show affection to Allah and His Messenger in your seeking nearness to Him through obedience and righteous deeds. It is also read as "illā mawaddatan fī al-qurbā."

﴿And whoever earns a good deed﴾ — that is, whoever acquires any good deed whatsoever, so it encompasses the affection for the near of kin as a primary inclusion. It is related from al-Suddī that it is the one intended. It has also been said: it was revealed concerning al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) and the affection for them (the Prophet's family) within it, ﴿We will increase for him therein﴾ — that is, in the good deed.

﴿Good (ḥusnan)﴾ — by multiplying the reward. It is also read "yazid," meaning "Allah will increase," and it is read "ḥusnā."

﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ — toward whoever sins.

﴿Appreciative (shakūr)﴾ — toward whoever obeys, by fully giving the reward and bestowing upon him an increase out of His grace.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 24:

﴿Or do they say﴾: rather, do they say?

﴿"He has invented"﴾: Muhammad.

﴿"a lie against Allah"﴾: by claiming prophethood and reciting the Qur'an. The hamzah (interrogative particle, the alif of interrogation) here is for rebuke and denunciation, as if it were said: Can they bring themselves to attribute to him, peace be upon him, who he is, such a thing as invention, especially invention against Allah, which is the greatest and most abominable of fabrications?

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿If Allah willed, He would seal up your heart﴾, this is an argument demonstrating the falsehood of what they say: that if he (peace be upon him) had invented against Allah the Exalted, Allah would certainly have prevented him from doing so. Its verification is that their claim that the Qur'an is an invention against Him is a statement by them that Allah the Exalted does not will its issuing from the Prophet (ﷺ), but rather wills its not issuing from him (p-31). And it necessarily follows that He would certainly prevent him from it. So it is as if it were said: If it were an invention against Him, the Exalted, He would will its not issuing from you. And if He willed that, He would seal up your heart, such that not a single meaning of it would occur to your mind, nor would you utter a single letter of it. Since the matter is not so, but rather revelation has come continuously, time after time, it becomes clear that this is from Allah the Exalted.

It has also been said: the meaning is, if He wills, He would make you one of those whose hearts are sealed, for no one dares to invent against Allah the Exalted except one who is like that. Its implication is the remoteness of such invention from one like him (peace be upon him), and that in remoteness it is like associating partners with Allah and entering among those whose hearts are sealed.

From Qatadah: ﴿He would seal up your heart﴾ means He would make you forget the Qur'an and cut off revelation from you; that is, if he had invented a lie against Allah, He would have done that to him. This is the meaning of what has been said: "If he lied against Allah, He would have made him forget the Qur'an."

It has also been said: ﴿He would seal up your heart﴾ means He would bind upon it with patience, so that their harm does not weigh heavily upon you.

﴿And Allah effaces falsehood and establishes truth by His words﴾: this is a resumptive sentence confirming the negation of invention; it is not conjoined to "He would seal up," as the explicit mention of the Glorious Name indicates, and the dropping of the waw (conjunction), as found in some codices, is for conformity to the wording, as in His saying: ﴿And man prays for evil﴾. That is: it is part of His habit, the Exalted, that He effaces falsehood and establishes truth by His revelation or by His decree, as in His saying: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth upon falsehood, and it crushes it﴾. So had it been an invention, as they claim, He would have annihilated and crushed it. Or it is a promise to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that He, the Exalted, will efface the falsehood in which they are, of slander and denial, and will establish the truth in which he is, through the Qur'an, or through His decree which cannot be averted, by granting him victory over them.

﴿Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾: so He applies to them the rulings befitting them, of effacement and establishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 25:

﴿He it is who accepts repentance from His servants﴾. Tawbah (repentance) is: returning from sins with remorse for them and resolve never to return to them ever again. Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, related that a Bedouin entered the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance," and he said takbir. When he finished his prayer, Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "O man, quickness of the tongue in seeking forgiveness is the repentance of liars, and this repentance of yours needs repentance." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, and what is repentance?" He said: "It is a term that applies to six meanings: for the past sins, remorse; for neglecting the obligations, making them up; restoring what was taken unjustly; making the self melt in obedience just as you had nurtured it in disobedience; making it taste the bitterness of obedience just as you had made it taste the sweetness of disobedience; and weeping in place of every laugh you laughed."

﴿And pardons evil deeds﴾, small and great, for whomever He wills.

﴿And He knows what you do﴾, whatever it is of good and evil, so He recompenses and overlooks according to what His will requires, which is founded on wisdom and benefits. It was also read "ta'malun" (what you do) with the letter ta'.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 26:

﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ That is: Allah responds to them (yastajib lahum), so the lam has been omitted, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when they measure out for them﴾, that is, measure out for them (kalu lahum). What is meant is the answering of their supplication and the rewarding of their obedience, for it is like a supplication and a request for what follows from it. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best supplication is 'Praise be to Allah'." Or it means: they respond to Allah by obedience when He calls them to it. It is related from Ibrahim ibn Adham that he was asked: "Why is it that we supplicate and are not answered?" He said: "Because He called you and you did not respond to Him." Then he recited: ﴿And Allah calls to the abode of peace.﴾

﴿And He increases them from His bounty﴾, beyond what they asked and deserved by the necessity of the promise.

﴿As for the disbelievers, there is a severe punishment for them﴾, in place of the reward and the abundant bounty that the believers have.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 27:

﴿And if Allah were to expand provision for His servants, they would surely rebel in the earth﴾. They would become arrogant and cause corruption therein out of insolence; or some of them would tyrannize over others through domination and overbearing, as is the way of human nature. The root meaning of baghy (transgression, rebellion) is seeking to exceed moderation in what is aimed at, whether in quantity or in quality.

﴿But He sends down in measure﴾, i.e., by a determined measure.

﴿whatever He wills﴾, namely to send down of it what His will requires.

﴿Indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾, encompassing the hidden and the manifest of their affairs. So He determines for each one of them, at every time of their lives, what befits their condition: He makes poor and makes rich, withholds and gives, restricts and expands, as the divine wisdom requires. Had He made them all rich, they would rebel; and had He made them all poor, they would perish. It is narrated that the people of the Suffah wished for wealth, and this verse was revealed. It was also said: it was revealed concerning the Arabs, who, when they were blessed with fertility, would fight one another, and when they suffered drought, would migrate in search of pasture.

﴿And He it is who sends down the rain﴾, i.e., the rain that brings them relief from drought. For this reason it is specified as the beneficial kind of rain. It was also read as "يُنْزِلُ" (from al-inzal).

﴿after they have despaired﴾, i.e., have lost hope in it. Restricting its sending to this circumstance, although it would be realized without this restriction too, is to call to mind the completeness of the blessing. It was also read with a kasra on the nun.

﴿and spreads His mercy﴾, i.e., the blessings and benefits of the rain in everything: the plain and the mountain, the plants and the animals. Or it means His wide mercy, which is ordered in what was mentioned, in an initial ordering.

﴿And He is the Protector﴾, who looks after His servants with kindness and by spreading mercy.

﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, who deserves praise for that, and no other.

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, in respect of the wonders of craftsmanship they embody, for they, by their very essence and attributes, indicate His great affairs.

﴿And what He has dispersed within them﴾ is a coordination (*ʿaṭf*) upon "the heavens" or upon "the creation."

﴿of living creature﴾: that is, of a living being, by way of naming the effect (*musabbab*) after its cause (*sabab*), or [it means] "what crawls upon the earth." Something that belongs specifically to one of two adjacent things may be attributed to both, as in His saying, ﴿From both of them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, whereas they only come forth from the saltwater. It has also been permitted that the angels, upon them be peace, may have a walking alongside their flying, so they are described as crawling. It is also possible that God creates in the sky living creatures who walk within it as humans walk upon the earth, as His saying indicates, ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾.

It has been narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Above the seventh heaven is a sea, the distance between its bottom and its top being like the distance between the heaven and the earth. Then above that are eight mountain goats, the distance between their knees and their hooves being like the distance between the heaven and the earth. Then above that is the Mighty Throne."

﴿And He is over their gathering﴾, that is, their assembling after resurrection for the reckoning. His saying, ﴿when He wills﴾, is connected to what precedes it, not to His saying ﴿is All-Powerful﴾ (p-33), for what is conditioned by will is His gathering, not His power. And *idhā* (إذا), when it carries the meaning of "time," enters the past tense just as it enters the present tense (*muḍāriʿ*).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 30:

﴿Whatever affliction befalls you﴾ — of whatever kind it may be.

﴿It is because of what your hands have earned﴾ — that is: it is your sins which you have acquired. The particle fa' (the "fa" of consequence, which introduces the apodosis) is used because "ma" is conditional (shartiyya), or because it contains the meaning of a condition. It has also been read without the fa', relying on what is already contained in the "ba'" (of causation, al-sababiyya) of the meaning of cause.

﴿And He pardons much﴾ — of the sins, so He does not punish for them. The verse is specific to the sinners, for what befalls others is due to other causes, among them that it exposes them to reward through patience in bearing it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 31:

﴿And you cannot escape within the earth﴾, (you cannot) escape what has been decreed against you of calamities, even if you flee to every refuge in its regions.

﴿And you have no protector other than Allah﴾, who would shield you from them.

﴿Nor any helper﴾, who would repel them from you.

{Wa min ayatihi al-jawar}: the ships that run.

{Fi al-bahr}: and it is read "al-jawari" (with the final vowel differing; a variant reading).

{Ka al-a'lam}: that is, like the mountains in general, not those upon which there is fire for guidance specifically.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 33:

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾ which He sends forth. It is also read "al-riyah" (the winds).

﴿So they become motionless on its back﴾ that is, they remain fixed on the surface of the sea, i.e., not running, not even moving at all.

﴿Indeed in that﴾ which has been mentioned of the ships that run at times and stand still at others, according to His will, may He be exalted.

﴿are signs﴾ great in themselves and numerous in count, indicating the aspects of Him, may He be exalted, that have been mentioned.

﴿for every steadfast, grateful one﴾ for everyone who restrains himself from turning toward what is not fitting, and who devotes his resolve to contemplating the signs of God, may He be exalted, and reflecting on His bounties; or, for every perfect believer, for faith is half patience and half gratitude.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 34:

﴿Or He destroys them for what they have earned﴾. It is coordinated (ʿatf) with "He stills" (yuskin), and the meaning is: if He wills, He stills the wind so that they remain motionless, or He sends it so that they drown by its violence. The attribution of the destruction (al-iyban) to them, although it is a state of "their people" (ahluhunna), is for emphasis and to convey awe (al-tahwil). The application of its ruling to the pardon in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿and He pardons much﴾, is because the meaning is: or He sends it so that He destroys some people and saves others by way of pardoning them. It has been read "wa-yaʿfu" (and He pardons) as a resumptive (isti'naf) clause.

﴿And that those who dispute concerning Our signs may know﴾ is coordinated (*'atf*, grammatical conjunction) with an implied cause (*'illah*, reason), such as "so that He may take vengeance upon them" and "so that He may know those who dispute..." and so on, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿and We will make him a sign for mankind﴾, and His words: ﴿and that We may teach him the interpretation of accounts﴾, and similar examples.

It is also read in the nominative (*raf'*), as a resumption (*isti'naf*, a new independent clause), and in the jussive (*jazm*), as coordinated with "*ya'fu*" (He pardons). The meaning then is: If He wills, He combines in one act the destruction of one people, the deliverance of another people, and the warning of a third people, ﴿they will have no place of escape﴾, i.e., no way of fleeing from the punishment. The clause is one from which the verb is suspended (*mu'allaq 'anha al-fi'l*, a construction in which the verb's operation is held in abeyance).

(p-34) ﴿So whatever you have been given of a thing﴾ — of what you desire and compete for.

﴿Then it is the enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ — i.e., it is its enjoyment, which you enjoy for the duration of your life.

﴿And what is with Allah﴾ — of the reward of the Hereafter.

﴿Is better﴾ in its essence, because its benefit is pure.

﴿And more lasting﴾ in time, since it does not cease nor perish.

﴿For those who believe and upon their Lord they rely﴾ — not upon anything else at all. The first relative clause, since it includes the meaning of a conditional (in that the giving of what they were given is a cause of enjoying it in the worldly life), has the fa' (then) entering its response, unlike the second. It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, gave away his wealth in charity, so a group of Muslims blamed him, and then this was revealed.

The commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who avoid the major sins (kaba'ir) of sin﴾, that is: the major sins of this kind.

﴿And the indecencies (fawahish), and when they are angry, they forgive﴾. Together with what follows it, this is a conjunction (ʿatf) with "those who believe", or a praise (madh) in the accusative (naṣb) or nominative (raf'), and the construction of "they forgive" with the pronoun as its predicate (khabar) is to indicate that they are the ones specially singled out for forgiveness at the time of anger, because of the rarity of attaining it. It has also been read as kabira al-ithm (singular), and it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that kabir al-ithm means: shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 38:

﴿And those who answer their Lord and establish the prayer﴾ It was revealed concerning the Ansar (the Helpers of Medina). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited them to faith, and they answered him.

﴿And their affair is [conducted by] consultation among themselves﴾ That is: they are people of consultation; they do not single out an opinion until they consult one another and reach agreement upon it. Before the Hijrah and after it, whenever a matter afflicted them, they would gather and consult.

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾ That is: in the way of good. The reason for separating this from its companion [i.e., the prayer] by mentioning consultation is that consultation takes place when they gather for the prayers.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 39:

﴿And those who, when tyranny afflicts them, they defend themselves.﴾ That is: they take retribution against those who oppress them, in accordance with what Allah the Exalted has made lawful for them, since they dislike being humiliated. This is a description of them with courage, after describing them with the rest of the essential virtues. This does not contradict their being described with forgiveness, for each of the two is a praiseworthy virtue in its own place and a blameworthy vice in the place of its counterpart. Forbearance toward the weak and toward the lapses of the noble is praiseworthy, whereas forbearance toward the domineering and toward the foolishness of the base is blameworthy, for it is an incitement to tyranny. On this is the saying of the one who said:

Poetry: "When you honour the noble, you make him your possession, / but if you honour the base, he becomes insolent."

Poetry: "Placing generosity in the place of the sword in matters of exaltedness / is as harmful as placing the sword in the place of generosity."

The Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾, is an explanation of the reason why retaliation is among the praiseworthy traits, despite it being in itself an injury to another, by indicating that the initiator is the one who did it to himself, for actions necessarily entail their requitals: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil. In it there is also a warning against transgression (hurmat al-ta'addi, the sanctity of not transgressing). The application of the term "evil" to the second is because it causes harm (tasu'u) to the one upon whom it descends.

﴿But whoever pardons﴾ the one who wronged him,

﴿and makes reconciliation﴾ between himself and the one who is hostile to him, through pardon and overlooking, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then suddenly the one between you and him is enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend﴾.

﴿His reward is with Allah﴾ is an indefinite promise, indicating the greatness of the status of the one promised and that it exceeds the customary limit.

﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾, those who initiate evil and those who transgress in retaliation.

Surah 42, verse 41:

﴿And whoever retaliates after he has been wronged﴾: that is, after he has been wronged. It has also been read this way.

﴿Those﴾: a demonstrative referring to "whoever" in respect of its meaning, just as the two pronouns referring to it are in respect of its wording.

﴿there is no blame upon them﴾: by way of reproach or punishment.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 42:

﴿Surely the way (of blame) is only against those who wrong people⦆ — that is, they begin harming them, or they exceed the bounds in retaliation.

﴿And they act insolently in the earth without right⦆ — that is, they behave arrogantly in it with tyranny and corruption.

﴿Those⦆ — the ones described with what has been mentioned of wronging and insolent transgression without right.

﴿For them is a painful punishment⦆ — because of their wronging and their transgression.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 43:

﴿And whoever is patient⁠﴾ over harm.

﴿and forgives⁠﴾ the one who wronged him, and does not seek retribution, and entrusts his affair to God Most High.

﴿Indeed, that⁠﴾ which has been mentioned of patience and forgiveness

﴿is surely among the steadfast resolves of affairs⁠﴾ That is: indeed, that is from it (i.e., from the steadfast resolves), and the predicate ("from it") has been omitted, relying on how evident it is, as in their saying: "Samn (ghee) is two manns for a dirham," and this applies to matters in which pardon does not lead to harm, as has been pointed out.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 44:

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him﴾, i.e., no helper who would take charge of him after Allah has forsaken him (khidhlan).

﴿And you will see the wrongdoers when they see the punishment﴾, i.e., when they see it. The use of the past tense (sighah al-madi) indicates the certainty of its occurrence.

﴿They say: Is there any way of return?﴾, i.e., any return (raj'ah) to the world.

﴿Is there any way [of return]?﴾ so that we may believe and do righteous deeds.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 45:

﴿And you will see them exposed to it﴾ i.e., to the Fire, which is indicated by the mention of the punishment (al-'adhab). The address in both places is to everyone who is capable of seeing.

﴿Humbled, abased from disgrace﴾ meaning: abject, diminished by what has befallen them.

﴿They look from a hidden glance﴾ i.e., their looking toward the Fire begins with a faint movement of their eyelids, like one who is being led to the sword and glances at it (al-mas'bur yanzuru ila al-sayf).

﴿And those who believed will say: Indeed, the losers﴾ i.e., those who truly embody (al-muttasifin bi-haqiqati) loss (al-khusran).

﴿Those who have lost themselves and their families﴾ by exposing themselves to the everlasting punishment.

﴿On the Day of Resurrection﴾ This may be a time-adverb for "have lost", in which case the statement refers to the worldly life (fi al-dunya), or for "will say", in which case the saying is on the Day of Resurrection, i.e., they say it when they see them in that state. The past tense form is used to indicate the certainty of its occurrence. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment﴾, it is either part of their own speech or a confirmation from God, exalted is He, of what they said.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 46:

﴿And they will have no allies to help them⁠﴾ by lifting the punishment from them.

﴿other than Allah⁠﴾ as they used to hope in the world.

﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no way⁠﴾ that would lead his conduct to salvation.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 47:

﴿Respond to your Lord﴾ when He calls you to faith through the tongue of His Prophet.

﴿Before there comes a Day which cannot be turned back from Allah﴾ That is: Allah will not turn it back after He has decreed it. This is on the reading that "min" (from) is connected to "maradd" (turning back); or [the meaning is]: before there comes from Allah a Day that cannot be averted.

﴿You will have no refuge that Day﴾ That is: no escape to which you can flee for refuge.

﴿And you will have no denial﴾ That is: no denying of what you have committed, because it is recorded in the pages of your deeds, and your limbs will bear witness against you.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 48:

﴿But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a watcher over them.﴾ This is a shift in the discourse (talwin lil-kalam) and a turning of it away from addressing people after commanding them to respond, and a directing of it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That is: if they do not respond and turn away from what you call them to, then We have not sent you as a guardian (raqib) and one who holds them to account (muhasib).

﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message).﴾ And you have done so.

﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us﴾ That is: a blessing of health, wealth and security.

﴿he rejoices in it.﴾ The term "man" (al-insan) is meant generically (al-jins), as indicated by His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if an evil befalls them﴾ That is: a affliction of sickness, poverty or fear.

﴿because of what their own hands have sent forth, then indeed man is ungrateful.﴾ Intensely ungrateful (baligh al-kufr), he forgets the blessing altogether, dwells on the affliction and magnifies it, and does not reflect on its cause; rather he claims that it befell him without his deserving it. The attribution of this trait to the human species, although it is a characteristic of the wicked (al-mujrimun), is because they predominate among individuals. The first conditional is introduced with "idha" (when) and the bestowal of the blessing is attributed to the royal "we" (nun al-'azamah) to alert that the conveying of blessing is certain to exist, frequent in occurrence, and that it is required by His essence. Likewise, the second is introduced with "in" (if), the affliction is attributed to an evil (sayyi'ah), and its cause is given as their deeds, to indicate the rarity of its occurrence and that it is far removed from being included among what is willed in itself. The placing of the apparent noun in place of the pronoun serves to record that this kind of people is marked by ingratitude for blessings.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 49:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Among the requirements of this is that He has the right of disposal over them and over everything in them as He wills, and among its scope is that He apportions blessing and affliction as He desires.

﴿He creates what He wills﴾ of what you know and of what you do not know.

﴿He bestows female [offspring] upon whom He wills﴾ from among the children.

﴿And He bestows male [offspring] upon whom He wills﴾ (p-37) from among them, without anyone having any part in that.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 50:

﴿Or He gives them in pairs﴾, that is: He joins the two kinds together and bestows both of them.

﴿males and females﴾. They said: the meaning of "He gives them in pairs" is that a woman gives birth to a boy and then a girl, or a girl and then a boy, or she gives birth to a male and a female as twins.

﴿And He makes whom He wills barren﴾. The meaning is: He makes the states of the servants with regard to offspring differ according to what His will requires. So He grants to some either one kind, male or female, or both kinds, and He makes others barren. Perhaps the females are mentioned first because they are more numerous, for the multiplication of progeny; or because the context of the verse is to show that what occurs is what His Exalted will is related to, not what human will is related to, and females are likewise; or because the discussion concerns trial, and the Arabs regard daughters as the greatest of trials; or to comfort the hearts of their fathers; or to preserve the rhyme (fawasil) of the verses, and for this reason the males were made definite; or to compensate for the delay, and the change of the conjunction in the third (ab, "or") is because it is the counterpart of what is shared between the two categories, while there is no need for it in the fourth, since it makes clear that it is the counterpart of what is shared among the preceding categories. It has been said: the purpose is to explain the states of the prophets, peace be upon them, for Shu'ayb and Lot were granted females, Abraham males, the Prophet ﷺ males and females, and Yahya and Isa were made barren.

﴿Indeed He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾, exceeding in knowledge and power, so He does what contains wisdom and benefit.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 51:

﴿And it is not for a human being﴾ That is: it is not right for any individual among mankind.

﴿that Allah should speak to him﴾ in any manner whatsoever.

﴿except by revelation﴾ That is: except by Him revealing to him, inspiring him, and casting into his heart, as He revealed to the mother of Musa (Moses) and to Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon them both, concerning the slaughter of his son. It has been narrated from Mujahid that Allah revealed the Zabur (Psalms) to Dawud (David), peace be upon him, into his breast. Or [it is] by Him causing him to hear His speech, which He creates in some bodies, without the hearer seeing the one who is speaking to him. This is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or from behind a veil﴾, for it is an illustration of Him by the condition of a king who is veiled, who speaks to some of his close associates from behind a curtain, so that he hears his voice but does not see his person, as He spoke to Musa and as He speaks to the angels, peace be upon them. Or [it is] by Him speaking to him through an intermediary, the angel, and this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or sends a messenger﴾ That is: an angel, ﴿who reveals﴾ by that messenger to the one to whom he is sent, who is the human messenger.

﴿by His permission﴾ That is: by His command, exalted is He, and His facilitation.

﴿what He wills﴾ to reveal to him. This is what takes place between Him, exalted is He, and the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, in most of their speech. It has been said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿wahyan (revelation)﴾ and His saying, exalted is He, ﴿aw yursila (or sends)﴾ are two verbal nouns (masdar) occupying the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿aw min wara'i hijab (or from behind a veil)﴾ is an adverbial phrase (zarf) occupying its position. The implied meaning is: it is not right that He should speak except as one who reveals, or as one who makes [him] hear from behind a veil, or as one who sends. It was also read as "aw yursilu" in the nominative, by supposing an implied subject (mubtada'). It is narrated that the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Will you not speak to Allah and look at Him, if you are a prophet, as He spoke to Musa and Musa looked at Him? For we will not believe until you do that." So he, peace be upon him, said: "Musa, peace be upon him, did not look at Allah, exalted is He." Then this was revealed. And from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah." Then she, may Allah be pleased with her, said: (p-38) "Did you not hear your Lord say—" and she recited this verse.

﴿Indeed He is Most High﴾ exalted above the attributes of created beings. The conversation between Him, exalted is He, and them cannot take place except in one of the modes mentioned.

﴿All-Wise﴾ He conducts His actions according to the course of wisdom, so He speaks at times through an intermediary and at other times without one, either by inspiration or by direct address.

﴿And thus﴾ means: in the same wondrous manner of revelation.

﴿We revealed to you a spirit (rūḥan) from Our command﴾ refers to the Qur'an, which stands to hearts as the spirit stands to bodies, since it gives them an everlasting life. It was also said that it refers to Jibril (peace be upon him). The meaning of his being revealed to him (peace be upon them both) is that He sent it to him with revelation (waḥy).

﴿You did not know﴾ before the revelation.

﴿What the Book was﴾ means: what it is.

﴿Nor faith﴾ means: faith in the details of what is contained within the Book of matters that reason cannot reach by itself, not faith in what reason and reflection can establish independently. For his knowledge of that, peace and blessings be upon him, is certainly beyond doubt.

﴿But We made it﴾ means: the spirit which We revealed to you.

﴿A light by which We guide whom We will﴾ means: its guidance.

﴿of Our servants﴾, and this is the one who directs his choice toward being guided by it. His, exalted is He, saying ﴿And indeed you guide﴾ is an affirmation of His guidance and an explanation of its manner. The object of "latahdī" (you guide) is omitted, relying on its being entirely evident: that is, ﴿And indeed you guide, by that light, whom We will to guide﴾.

﴿to a straight path﴾ is Islam and the rest of the sacred laws (sharā'i') and rulings (aḥkām). It was read "latuhdā" (ḥuṭhdā), meaning "that Allah may guide you," and it was read "latadʿū" (you call).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 42, verse 53:

﴿Ṣirāṭ Allāh﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the first [noun, al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm], and its attribution to the Divine Name (al-ism al-jalīl), followed by its qualification with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Him to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, is for the magnification of His station, the affirmation of its straightness, and the emphasis of the obligation of following it. For the fact that all the existing things within them belong to Him, exalted is He, in creation, dominion and disposal, is of that which necessitates this in the most complete necessitation.

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾: that is, the affairs of everything in them [the heavens and the earth], entirely, not to anyone else. Therein is, from the promise to those guided to the Straight Path and the warning to those who go astray from it, what is not hidden. From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Whoever recites Surah Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf, he is among those for whom the angels send blessings, and seek forgiveness, and ask mercy for him﴾.
